newsitem.title: USA: Bourbon fuels Kentucky distillery fire.
newsitem.headline: Bourbon fuels Kentucky distillery fire.

text.p: A stubborn fire fueled by bourbon and high winds that sent rivers of flaming alcohol cascading across a highway and into a creek continued to burn on Friday at the Heaven Hills distillery, authorities said.
No one was injured in the blaze that ignited on Thursday afternoon but 10 homes were evacuated. The cause of the fire was not known.

The fire was contained but not before it destroyed seven of 25 warehouses holding bourbon being aged in wooden casks. It also gutted the Heaven Hills distillery, which is 35 miles (56 km) south of Louisville.

Witnesses reported that burning whiskey flowed like lava down a hillside, across a highway and into a creek after several warehouses collapsed in flames. Strong winds helped spread the blaze, which was being investigated by the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.
All the company's 350 employees were called into work on Friday. Most work in the undamaged bottling plant.

"There's plenty of good quality bourbon available now and in the future," said Max Shapira, executive vice president of Heaven Hills, which makes the premium 12-year-old Elijah Craig brand and the Evan Williams brand. The company, which had $150 million in sales last year, also sells gin, vodka, rum and other types of liquor.

Nelson County, in which Bardstown is located, is known as the bourbon capital of the world with several distilleries in the region, attracted by iron-free water and white oak forests used to make the casks.
